title: tool loop: truncated-recovery widens main cap but not wrap-up cap
description:
Repro: 'review the file structure and summarize its purpose'. Directory-summary wrap-up round needs > 384 tokens; model truncates. _diagnose_bail returns 'truncated', current_max_tokens doubles (1024→2048), bail_retries decrements, loop retries. But the round-budget calc is `round_max_tokens = min(current_max_tokens, wrap_up_max_tokens) if tools_already_ran` — wrap_up_max_tokens stays at 384. So every retry re-truncates at the same spot, and with _BAIL_RETRIES_PER_TURN=2 the user sees 3 different partial summaries streamed, each cut at ~384 tokens.

Fix: also widen wrap_up_max_tokens on truncated recovery. Mirror current_max_tokens: track current_wrap_up_max_tokens, double it in the 'truncated' branch. Test: scripted adapter that returns truncated reply on round 1 then non-truncated on round 2; assert the second wrap-up round got a wider max_tokens.
close_reason: Fixed. current_wrap_up_max_tokens now tracked alongside current_max_tokens and widened on the 'truncated' recovery branch. Without this, wrap-up rounds that overran the 384-token cap would re-truncate at the same spot because round_max_tokens = min(current_max_tokens, wrap_up_max_tokens) kept clamping to 384 even after current_max_tokens doubled. Test: test_wrap_up_cap_widens_on_truncated_recovery asserts the retry gets 256 tokens (up from initial 128).

title: main model fabricates web-sourced prose after weak router-prelude result
description: Repro (see harness-cx2): 'tell me about origin of Jehovah's Witnesses religion' routes to search_facts (weak hits [~0.36]), then the main model emits prose that reads like web search results without ever calling search_web. The original bug frame was 'TUI hides later tool calls' — investigation showed the orchestrator + CLI renderer both emit/display every call (added 5 regression tests: tests/test_tool_loop.py::test_loop_observer_receives_events_for_{every_round,each_call_in_one_round}; tests/test_cli_helpers.py::test_render_tool_event_*). What actually happened in the repro was pure fabrication: the main model saw low-confidence facts, its 'let me search the web' preamble got eaten by _TOOL_INTENT_RE suppression, and then it continued on to invent well-shaped web-result prose that didn't trip _FABRICATED_SEARCH_RE (no numbered 'here are the results', no placeholder domains). Possible mitigations: (a) tighten fabrication regex to catch narrative-style invented facts with named sources; (b) when router-prelude returns low-confidence hits, nudge the main model to explicitly call search_web; (c) raise the router's search_facts min_confidence so weak hits don't anchor a hallucination. Suggest trying (b) first — least invasive.

title: TUI shows only the first tool call per turn; subsequent tool invocations hidden
description:
When the agent chains multiple tools in a single turn, only the first tool call is rendered in the chat TUI. Later tool invocations run and influence the final reply but are invisible to the user, making it hard to audit what actually happened.

Repro:
  you › tell me about the origin of jehovah's witnesses religion
  airton ›
  → routed to search_facts
  🔧 Recall facts ({'query': "origin of Jehovah's Witnesses", 'k': 5, 'min_confidence': 0.8})
     ✓ [0.365] ... (weak hits)
  [model then runs a web search and returns web results, but no 🔧 line is shown for it]
  <final reply contains clearly-web-sourced results>

Expected: every tool call in the loop emits its own 🔧 label + args + compact result line, in order.

Likely location: orchestrator/tool_loop.py display-label path, or the CLI renderer that consumes tool events. Probably a 'first call only' guard or a display-state variable that isn't reset per-iteration.

Fix scope:
- Audit the tool loop: confirm each iteration's tool_calls are emitted to the renderer.
- Check whether the renderer dedupes on tool name, session, or missing event ID.
- Add a test: fake adapter that emits two sequential tool_calls, assert both appear in captured output.
close_reason: Not a renderer or orchestrator bug. Added 5 regression tests proving every tool_call_start event reaches the observer and every observer event renders a 🔧 line — across multi-round, multi-call-per-round, and router-prelude scenarios. Extracted _render_tool_event from the chat-command closure to make it testable. Root cause of the repro was fabrication: the main model hallucinated web-sourced prose after the router's weak search_facts result, without ever calling search_web. Refiled as harness-cwx.

title: Phraseology lint: per-section verb-anchor re-rank for cluster #3 retrieval misroutes

Cluster #3 failure pattern: short numeric utterances (e.g. 'AMERICAN ONE TWENTY THREE, SQUAWK SEVEN FIVE ZERO ZERO') retrieve §2-4-17 (Numbers Usage) instead of the section that actually governs them (§10-2-6 Hijack), because the corpus's PHRASEOLOGY example blocks contain similar spelled-form numbers and §2-4-17 has the most numeric content by token count. Examples: SQUAWK → §10-2-6, 7500 → §10-2-6, MAYDAY → §10-1-1, REDUCE SPEED → §5-7-2, MAINTAIN (... KNOTS) → §5-7-2, CONTACT → §2-1-17, LINE UP AND WAIT → §3-9-4, CLEARED FOR TAKEOFF → §3-9-10, CLEARED TO LAND → §3-10-5, LOW ALTITUDE ALERT → §2-1-6, TRAFFIC ALERT → §2-1-6, TRAFFIC, (clock position) → §2-1-21. Implementation: (a) author character/airton_c1/corpus/verb_anchors.yaml (section → list of distinctive verbs/code phrases). (b) Modify lint_utterance to detect verb-anchor matches in the utterance and boost matching sections in the candidate slate (e.g. add a virtual hit at rank 0 for the matched §, OR re-rank the existing hits by verb-overlap score). (c) Cite-grounding gate still filters ungrounded picks. (d) Validate by re-running 'harness eval phraseology --compare-baseline'. Expected lift: cluster #3 cases (han_speed_*, emerg_hijack_*, han_contact_*) flip from §2-4-17 to correct §; canonical cases unchanged because their verb-anchors are already grounded by retrieval. Out-of-scope: ingest-side synonym maps (precision risk per harness-ajn discipline).

title: Phraseology lint: strip phonetic digit-words from retrieval query (cluster #3 retrieval misroutes)
description: Phase-1 product-gate work for harness-q35t. Baseline post-rubric-fix (kl0w) sits at 14/40 = 35% combined; ~45pp shy of the 80% gate. Failure cluster #3 dominates the residual: short utterances with phonetic-spelled numeric tokens overwhelm hybrid retrieval and pull wrong sections. Examples: 'SQUAWK SEVEN FIVE ZERO ZERO' retrieves §2-4-17 (Numbers Usage) instead of §10-2-6 (Hijack); 'REDUCE SPEED TO TWO FIVE ZERO' retrieves §2-4-17 instead of §5-7-2 (Speed Adjustment); 'CONTACT DEPARTURE ONE TWO THREE POINT FOUR' loses §2-1-17 to numeric-token chapter. Fix: in src/harness/tools/phraseology_lint.py::lint_utterance, preprocess the retrieval query (NOT the user message shown to the model) by stripping standalone phonetic digit words (ZERO, ONE, ..., NINE, NINER, TEN, ELEVEN, ..., NINETY, HUNDRED, THOUSAND, POINT). The model still sees the original utterance for classification; only retrieval gets the cleaned query. Hypothesis: 'AMERICAN ONE TWENTY THREE, SQUAWK SEVEN FIVE ZERO ZERO' → 'AMERICAN, SQUAWK' lets §10-2-6 win the candidate set. Validate by re-running 'harness eval phraseology --compare-baseline' and snapshotting a new baseline if combined accuracy lifts.
close_reason: Investigated, both query-side mods regressed combined accuracy below the 35% baseline; reverted. Approach 1 (strip phonetic-digit tokens from retrieval query): -5pp combined (35→30%). Hijack/squawk cluster won (9 case improvements including emerg_hijack_verify_canonical, emerg_hijack_wrong_code, emerg_traffic_advisory_canonical) but 9 canonical landing/handoff cases regressed (arr_landing_canonical, arr_pilot_oos, han_pilot_freq_oos etc.) — stripping was too aggressive on cases where retrieval was already working. Hypothesis: short stripped queries (e.g. 'RUNWAY CLEARED TO LAND') give BM25/dense too little signal vs originals that match the corpus's spelled-form examples. Approach 2 (augment: original + stripped concatenated): -7.5pp combined (35→27.5%). Citation accuracy actually rose +2.5pp but verdict crashed -12.5pp — the model saw different candidates from the merged retrieval and verdicts shifted. Both reverted. Working theory for cluster #3: the corpus's PHRASEOLOGY blocks contain spelled-form examples that match short utterances on dense embedding; the §2-4-17 (Numbers Usage) chapter wins on TOTAL token volume of phonetic digits not because it's semantically right but because it has the most numeric content. Future angles to try (NOT this bead): (a) per-section synonym/anchor map keyed to short utterance verbs ('SQUAWK' → §10-2-6, '7500' → §10-2-6 hijack, etc.); (b) k bump from 8 to 12-16 with cite-grounding gate filtering; (c) two-stage retrieval: hybrid pull top-K, then re-rank by section-specific keyword overlap with the utterance's verb-class. Documented in character/airton_c1/phraseology_progress.md.

title: airton_c1 lane F-prime auto-replace: cite-grounding catcher actuator
description: Phase-1.6 child of harness-7wju. Lane F-prime detect-only shipped under harness-11ha (Run 12, 2026-04-26). Module src/harness/persona/cite_grounding.py + --cite-ground flag on eval atc. Detection works: 2/2 real wrong-cite fabs caught (controller_same_runway_arrival_lay_time §3-10-4, controller_hijack_squawk §10-2-5 → suggested §10-2-6 exact). But 3 false positives on voice-sample-anchored lay variants (wake_turb_lay §2-1-19, missed_approach_lay §5-10-11, handoff_lay §5-4-5). FP budget too high to auto-replace as a hard filter. This bead tracks the actuator design: how to auto-replace ungrounded cites without nuking the voice-sample-carried lay-variant cases. Candidate strategies: (1) voice-anchored evidence weighting — skip rank check when cited section appears in any canonical voice sample's gold AND the user query is cosine-similar to that sample's prompt (not just the gold's anchor); (2) cosine sanity check on (question, cited_section_principle) — if absolute cosine high enough, override the rank check; (3) per-section-class threshold (lay vs jargon queries get different K); (4) re-roll with nudge ('§X-Y-Z is about T — does that match the question?') instead of silent replace. Decision criterion: Phase-1.6 auto-replace must keep all 26 currently-passing cases passing AND flip ≥1 of the 2 caught fabs. Acceptance: eval atc ≥27/29 = 93.1% with --cite-ground --replace, no regressions vs detect-only run.

title: airton_c1 lane F-prime: post-rewrite cite-grounding catcher (Phase-1.6 child)
description: Phase-1.6 child of harness-7wju. Structural fix for 'real but wrong section' cite fabrications — orthogonal to voice-sample farming. title: hybrid RRF: BM25 hits land below cosine floor → topical bleed
description: store/_hybrid.py fuses BM25 (FTS5) + dense cosine via reciprocal-rank fusion. RRF preserves rank order regardless of absolute similarity, so a BM25 lexical hit on a repeated word ('junior', 'stack') can rank an old, semantically-unrelated row into the top-K even when its dense cosine is well below the configured min_score. Result: stale memory leaks into queries that share only surface tokens. Investigate: (a) apply min_score floor on the fused score (not just dense); (b) require BM25 hits to also clear a soft cosine threshold; (c) document the trade-off and gate via --memories-threshold semantics. Reproduce: search 'junior' against the local episodic store and inspect what comes back at score >0.5 vs raw cosine.
close_reason: Added bm25_min_score gate to EpisodicStore.search + SemanticStore.search hybrid path. Default = max(min_score - 0.15, 0.0). Soft floor lets identifier queries keep working; common-word lexical bleed gets cut. 5 new tests via steerable axis-token embedder.

title: Tool-loop failure corpus + per-catcher attribution eval
description:
## Why

tool_loop.py is 731 lines with a growing stack of hallucination catchers (fabricated tool-call success, fabricated search results, bare tool-intent, quoted-snippet numbered lists, paired meta-confirm, ab Remembered-receipts, period-Captured, fake bead-ids, bail_retry, fabrication-exhaustion fallback). Recent commits (bec4578, 162b41d, 828effc, 34f34cf) keep adding patches. No eval pins which catcher saves which class of failure, so we cannot tell pruning-safe layers from load-bearing ones, and cannot compare a rearchitect against the current stack.

Existing benches (bench_tool_use, bench_router) measure throughput, not fabrication correctness. Router eval exists (character/<name>/router_eval.yaml) and is the template to copy.

## What

1. Capture a failure corpus from real session transcripts + the known hallucination shapes each catcher was added for. Fixture file: character/airton/tool_loop_eval.yaml. Each scenario:
   - messages: input turn(s)
   - tool_set / router mode / model (small + main, both mockable via echo-adapter scripted replies)
   - expected: final reply must/must-not contain, must-not claim tool success, must-not emit fake bead-id, etc.
   - label: which catcher class it stresses (e.g. "fabricated-remembered-receipt")

2. New command: `uv run harness eval tool-loop [--json]` scoring pass/fail per scenario with the label grouping so we see per-catcher coverage.

3. Attribution harness: run the fixture with each catcher individually disabled (env flag or param) and record the pass-rate delta. Output a table: catcher → scenarios it uniquely saves → scenarios where it is redundant with another catcher.

4. Commit the baseline numbers in the eval output so any rearchitect PR has a concrete target.

## Out of scope

- Actually rewriting the orchestrator. This task produces the measurement rig only.
- Adding new catchers. Document-and-measure, do not patch.

## Done when

- Fixture has >= 15 scenarios covering every catcher currently in tool_loop.py (grep for the catcher comments/labels to enumerate).
- `harness eval tool-loop` runs green on main and the per-catcher attribution table is printed.
- Test under tests/ pins fixture shape + CLI wiring (mirror tests/test_router_eval.py).
close_reason: Shipped: 19-scenario fixture, harness eval tool-loop CLI, per-catcher attribution, 13 new tests. Baseline 100% pass; 4 catchers uniquely load-bearing (truncated, unparseable, paired_meta_confirm_strip, duplicate_call), 7 share fabrication_fallback backstop. Follow-up worth considering: add retry-recovery scenarios (good reply after bail) so text-shape catchers register unique_saves independent of the fallback.

title: [bug] duplicate-call nudge misreads as success after a failed call
description:
Reproduced in live ab session 2026-04-18 while running pre-patch bd_adapter (see commit f4e57ae). Flow:

1. Model emits capture(...) tool call.
2. Tool fails (bd command failed — unrelated: the --add-label vs --labels bug).
3. Model retries with IDENTICAL args.
4. Orchestrator deduplicates → emits ToolResult(success=True, output=_DUPLICATE_CALL_NUDGE).
5. Model reads 'Result is unchanged from the earlier tool message' + success=True and hallucinates 'The task has been captured.'

Root cause: the dedup nudge flags success=True regardless of whether the earlier call succeeded. The model's last tool observation is the failure, but the dedup feedback frames it as a duplicate of a successful prior call.

Proposed fix:

Track the ToolResult of each unique call this turn in seen_calls instead of just the key. On a duplicate, re-emit the stored result (preserving success + output) rather than a fixed nudge. The nudge can still prepend as a suffix: '[duplicate — <prior outcome>]'.

Additional guardrail: when the stored result has success=False, make the dedup result's output quote the error so the model cannot paraphrase the outcome as 'captured' / 'done'.

Lives in src/harness/orchestrator/tool_loop.py around line 545-565. Tests: tests/test_tool_loop.py — add a case where two identical calls where the first fails, then the second dedupes with the failure preserved.

Out of scope for this issue: why the model retried with identical args after a failure (separate bug; likely small-model behavior, investigate later).

title: tool loop: short-circuit duplicate tool calls within a turn
description:
Repro: prompt 'review the file structure and summarize its purpose'. Model emits summary prose + list_dir({'path': '', 'recursive': true, 'include_hidden': false}) in the same reply. The orchestrator records the prose as assistant history and executes list_dir. Result unchanged. Model emits another summary + identical list_dir call. Loop continues across rounds, each emitting a duplicate summary and re-running list_dir with the same args, until max_rounds or the small model finally stops. User sees the same prose three times and three identical 🔧 list_dir lines.

Fix: track a per-turn set of (tool_name, canonical-json(args)) in run_tool_loop. When the model re-emits an identical call:
- Skip execution (no re-run).
- Emit a new tool_call_deduped event so the CLI shows it happened but didn't run again.
- Append a tool-role message: '[duplicate call — result unchanged; give the user your final answer now, no more tool calls]' so the model sees the nudge next round.

Also seed the set with the router-prelude call (if any) so a model that re-invokes the router's tool gets short-circuited too.

Tests:
- Same call across two rounds → executed once, deduped second.
- Same call twice in one ModelReply → executed once, deduped second.
- Different args to same tool → both executed.
- Router prelude + model re-invoke → model's call is deduped.

Tradeoff: treats legitimate repeated-poll patterns as redundant. Acceptable at this scale; can add a force=True escape later if a real use case shows up.

description:

title: Router parser: treat string 'null' as Python None

close_reason: Parser now folds literal 'null' / 'none' / 'NULL' / '  None  ' strings to Python None in _coerce_intent. Hermes-3-3B sometimes emits the word instead of real JSON null; previously these scored as tool_name='null' (a string) and misfired the eval. 1 new parse test covers the variants.

description:

title: Orchestrator: inject synthetic tool-call when router returns intent
description:
Extend run_tool_loop to accept an optional router: Router | None. Before the first adapter call:
1. If router is None -> current behavior.
2. Else call router.classify(last_user_message, registry.specs()).
3. If intent.tool_name is set AND exists in registry AND args validate against the spec schema -> append a synthetic assistant ChatMessage carrying that ToolCall, execute the tool (via the existing confirm/observe path), append the tool result, then let the main model wrap up.
4. Else (null or validation failure) -> fall through to normal tool loop.

Emit a new ToolLoopEvent kind="router_intent" so CLI can surface 'routed to search_web' inline. Tests cover: happy-path (intent -> tool ran -> wrap-up), null passthrough, bad-schema passthrough, nonexistent-tool passthrough.

title: Epic: intent router — small-model pre-pass for tool routing
description:
Add a small secondary model (Qwen 2.5 1.5B Instruct 4-bit) that runs BEFORE the main model for every turn and decides tool+args. When it returns an intent, the orchestrator injects a synthetic assistant tool-call turn, executes the tool, and hands the main model a single wrap-up round — no fabrication-and-retry rounds. When it returns null or unparseable, fall through to the normal tool loop.

- Router model: mlx-community/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct-4bit (~1GB RAM; same tokenizer family as main Qwen).
- Scope: tool routing only (no persona/skip/meta decisions).
- Advisory not blocking: unparseable output -> fall through, never fail the turn.
- Opt-in via --router flag; default off so we can bench against baseline.

Why now: 7B-4bit fabricates instead of calling search_web (harness-j1d). A small router sidesteps the problem entirely and scales to multi-user gateways without paying 3 rounds of 7B inference per misfire.

title: airton_c1 synonyms Phase 1: suggester + ablative tester scripts
description:
Phase 1 of the synonym management plan (see character/airton_c1/synonyms_policy.md). Two scripts:

(1) scripts/suggest_synonyms.py — for each fixture case in atc_retrieval_baseline.json at rank > 3 OR hard miss: fetch the expected chunk's body from the store, call a small model (router-tier Hermes 3B) with prompt 'given this query and this chunk, propose 3-5 lay-form phrases that would help the query find the chunk', emit a YAML draft block per case to stdout. (2) scripts/test_synonyms.py — takes a YAML file (one or more proposed entries), provisions a scratch DB if any entry is for synonyms.yaml (shared/ingest-side; needs re-ingest), runs eval atc-retrieval --json, diffs per-case ranks vs current baseline. Output verdict per entry: LIFT (target cases improve, no other regress), MIXED (some improve some regress), DEAD (no impact), HARMFUL (regression). Includes --ablate flag that walks every existing entry and tests with-without to detect dead entries.

Workflow becomes:
  1. uv run python scripts/suggest_synonyms.py > /tmp/suggested.yaml
  2. # human edits — picks/refines entries
  3. uv run python scripts/test_synonyms.py /tmp/suggested.yaml
  4. # if LIFT: paste into the right yaml file, commit

Acceptance: both scripts ship with tests using a scripted adapter (no live MLX) for the suggester, and a synthetic chunks dir for the tester. Demonstrate the suggester reaches the same answers (or close) as the manual Phase 0 fixes for missed_approach_lay and handoff_lay. title: airton_c1 retrieval Fix D: domain-tuned embedder swap benchmark
description: Most expensive option under epic harness-rhto. Evaluate swapping default embedder (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, 384-dim) for a larger / domain-closer alternative. Candidates: BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 (1024-dim, same family), intfloat/e5-large-v2, or a domain fine-tune on the JO 7110.65 corpus (last-resort). Benchmarks required: (1) atc_eval.yaml recall@5 before/after; (2) 2026-04-24 regression cases; (3) RAM delta (bench_ram.py) — bge-large adds ~1GB vs bge-small, tight on 32GB Mac; (4) embed latency delta (matters for ingest + per-turn retrieval); (5) re-embed cost one-time (scripts/atc_ingest.py runtime). Gate: only ship if Fix B + Fix C combined don't hit ≥90% recall on the expanded eval set. If gate fails, document the empirical recall ceiling and park the embedder swap as 'measured, not pursued'. Priority P3 because it's a last-resort — Fix B/C should close the gap cheaper. 2–3 day estimate if pursued, plus LoRA-fine-tune branch if bge-large insufficient.
notes:
PROMOTED to lane epic on 2026-04-25 after harness-hvu1 (Fix C LLM query expansion) closed with mixed/negative result — 3B Hermes lacks JO 7110.65 domain knowledge to emit useful jargon-space rewrites. Embedder fix is now the highest-leverage retrieval lane.

LANE STRUCTURE:
1. Off-the-shelf benchmark — sweep tier-1 candidates (bge-large, mxbai-large, bge-m3, nomic-embed-text) via scripts/bench_embedder.py. Stop at the first that clears the +15 pp recall@5 gate vs the BGE-small baseline.
2. Fine-tune fallback — only if the OTS sweep doesn't close the gap. LoRA on the strongest OTS candidate or full FT on bge-small. Requires synthetic-pair training data + a held-out eval split.

GATE (ship-as-default):
- ≥ +15 pp recall lift on @1/@3/@5 vs static-only BGE-small baseline (currently 73.7 / 89.5 / 89.5 / 100 on 19 cases).
- No regression on recall@10.
- Ingest seconds ≤ 3× baseline; peak RSS ≤ +1.5 GB.

title: Architectural: chunked output / model-splitting when wrap-ups regularly exceed ~4k tokens
description: Today: _MAX_TOKENS_CEILING is a 32k anti-runaway guard in orchestrator/tool_loop.py; wrap_up_max_tokens defaults to 1024 and auto-widens on truncation (capped at the ceiling). This is enough headroom that no single reply should truncate in practice — but it's a single-shot generation model. When wrap-up replies routinely want more than ~4k tokens (long research summaries, multi-file code edits, long creative writing, big report rewrites) we hit a wall before we hit the ceiling: MLX Qwen 2.5 7B on M4 Pro generates ~40-60 tok/s, so a 4k reply takes ~70-100s and an 8k reply feels broken. Retool options when that day comes: (a) chunked/streaming output — model produces an outline then per-section expansion, with partials persisted as we go so a crash mid-generation doesn't lose the whole reply; (b) model-splitting — a planner/critic persona writes the outline on a fast small model, a detail persona fills sections on the big model, composition is concatenated; (c) swap the wrap-up model for a faster one per-turn (adapter swap mid-turn). Trigger to act: once transcripts show repeated truncation-widen events even with the raised ceiling, or once users regularly Ctrl-X wrap-ups for being too slow. Not urgent — putting this bead down so the decision point isn't forgotten.
